jobs.title: Underground Mine Engineer Intern (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

The position is intended to provide a university student studying mining engineering or a related discipline with practical experience in underground mine engineering. The intern will assist the Technical Services team with mine design, ventilation, short- and medium-range mine planning, production support, cycle-time data collection, analysis, and special projects while consistently demonstrating Kinross values.

Essential Functions

1.  Assists mine engineers with underground development and production designs, including layouts for headings, ramps, accesses, stopes, drill patterns, services, and supporting infrastructure under appropriate supervision.
2.  Supports short- and medium-range mine planning by updating designs, quantities, equipment assumptions, activity durations, and schedule inputs using approved planning criteria.
3.  Assists ventilation personnel with underground ventilation surveys, including airflow, pressure, temperature, and environmental data collection, and helps maintain ventilation records and plans.
4.  Collects underground operating-cycle data for drilling, charging, blasting, re-entry, mucking, hauling, ground support, backfilling, and related activities using approved observation and data-capture methods.
5.  Assists with special projects such as haulage studies, equipment productivity reviews, development advance analysis, stope-cycle reviews, infrastructure trade-offs, and ventilation or mine-plan optimization.
6.  Compiles, validates, organizes, and summarizes engineering and operational data using spreadsheets, databases, dashboards, mine-planning software, and other approved systems.
7.  Works collaboratively with mine engineering, ventilation, geology, geotechnical engineering, survey, operations, maintenance, and other site personnel to complete assigned work and communicate findings.
8.  Conducts time-and-motion observations underground and records timestamps, delays, travel distances, equipment interactions, and operating conditions without interfering with production activities.
9.  Assists with comparing actual cycle performance against planning assumptions and prepares clear summaries of variances, recurring delays, and potential improvement opportunities for engineering review.
10.  Updates mine plans, sections, drawings, quantities, presentations, and planning documentation under the direction of qualified engineering personnel.
11.  Participate in underground inspections, planning meetings, pre-shift coordination, workplace examinations, and task-level risk assessments applicable to assigned engineering work.
12.  Compliance with all company policies and procedures including, but not limited to safety, environmental, confidentiality and code of conduct. 
13.  Meets or exceeds established performance expectations set by management.
14.  Consistently exercises discretion and judgment in job performance.
15.  Works without risk or harm to self and others. 
16.  Punctuality and regular attendance required.
17.  Performs other related functions as assigned by supervisor.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1.  Must possess a professional attitude toward responsibilities.
2.  Must be able to work with little or no direct supervision and work well with others.
3.  Must be able to work in a safe manner and adhere to RMGC safety standards.
4.   Possesses good communication and interpersonal skills. 
5.  General understanding of mining engineering principles and an interest in underground mine design, scheduling, ventilation, equipment productivity, and production systems.
6.  Working knowledge of computers and common word-processing, spreadsheet, database, and presentation software; exposure to mine-planning, CAD, ventilation-modeling, scheduling, GIS, or data-visualization software is an asset.
7.  Strong verbal, written, analytical and persuasive skills and the ability to interact effectively with all levels of employees and management.
8.  Ability to work independently when appropriate and collaboratively as a member of a multidisciplinary technical and operations team.
9.  Demonstrates strong analytical, organizational, data-management, problem-solving, and technical writing skills.
10.  Currently enrolled in a mining engineering or related bachelor’s degree program, with at least two years of university coursework preferred; 0-2 years of relevant engineering, mining, construction, or industrial experience preferred.
11.  Must be 18 years old and presently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. 
12.  Requires valid driver’s license.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•  Adheres to all safety and environmental considerations.
•  Have a strong commitment to safe working practices. 
•  Wears required Personal Protective Equipment at all times in underground, surface production, office, shop, and other designated work areas.
•  Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions. 
•  Follows operating procedures and comply with all regulatory requirements. 
•  Must be able and willing to work underground and travel through active mine workings in accordance with site access, training, and escort requirements.
•  Must maintain situational awareness around mobile equipment, blasting boundaries, ventilation controls, ground conditions

jobs.title: Chief Geotechnical Engineer (Fort Knox, AK, US)
jobs.description:
Located approximately 26 miles from the City of Fairbanks, Fort Knox is a centre of excellence for the Company as one of the few cold weather heap leach facilities in the world.

Fort Knox

celebrated its 25-year anniversary

in 2021, and has produced over 8.5 million ounces since it began operation. In 2020, Kinross acquired Manh Choh – a project expected to commence production in 2024 and process ore at Fort Knox.

Fort Knox prioritizes being a strong contributor to the State and local communities, and since 2001, has helped support more than 300 community partners and has contributed more than US$25 million to the Alaska Mental Health Trust.

Job Description

The Kinross - Fort Knox Technical Services team is seeking an experienced and dynamic Chief Geotechnical Engineer to lead the geotechnical department at the Fort Knox Gold Mine open pit.  Reporting to the Technical Services Manager, this position will provide support in all aspects of geotechnical engineering.

Responsible for providing geotechnical engineering support to the department to ensure that the mine functions effectively and safely with minimal impacts to the business.  Develop site geotechnical programs to meet or exceed industry standards.  Responsible for carrying out a full range of engineering functions.  To be familiar with and understand the principles of the environment policy and also to maintain and support procedures and work practices aimed at preventing accidents or injuries.

Job Responsibilities

Develop and implement geotechnical design criteria to support safe and optimal mine operations.

Plan and manage the installations of mine-wide geotechnical and hydrology monitoring systems.

Advise mine planning and operations personnel on geotechnical issues relating to production, drilling, blast, dewatering, and mine design.

Proactively perform site inspections, prepare operational mitigation plans, and manage geotechnical issues.

Plan, develop, and track expenses against the department budget including geotechnical and hydrology data collection and drilling programs.

Coordinate with the Water Manager in planning the hydrology program to ensure adequate instrumentation exists for monitoring pore pressures and phreatic surfaces relative to mine design targets.

Manage contracts and coordinate with geotechnical consultants to ensure high quality work products are developed, design criteria are clearly understood and effectively implemented, recommendations are optimized based on operational performance.

Perform geotechnical investigations and back analysis using geotechnical software.

In coordination with the Geology team, plan the collection, analysis, and interpretation of geotechnical data.

Ensure a sound geotechnical model covering mine geology, geological structures, rock mass quality and hydrogeology is built and updated through collection, analysis and interpretation of geotechnical data.

Generate monthly geotechnical & project management summaries and/or reports for use in company reporting.

Perform project management duties, including, but not limited to: contract review, bid award, cost estimation, schedule tracking, and reporting.

Effectively communicate anticipated geotechnical outcomes.

Maintain, update, and ensure compliance with the Ground Control Management Plan (GCMP)

Ensure that all reporting requirements and licensing conditions by regulatory bodies are met.

Supervise, train, and mentor junior engineers, geologists and technicians in all aspects of geotechnical engineering.

Be available for on-call support duties shared within the department.

Punctuality and regular attendance is required.

Maintain accurate records and files.

Perform other duties as required.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or Geology with industry related discipline such as, or similar to, Geotechnical, Mining, Geological, Structural, or Economic Geology is required.

Candidates should have at least 7 to 12 years of mining experience in large scale open-pit metal mining.

Thorough understanding of open-pit mining operations as well as a general understanding of milling operations and mine maintenance.

Practical experience with advanced geotechnical monitoring instruments and techniques

Must have a high level of computer literacy with specialized mining software. Experience with MineSight, Rocscience software packages, and WellCAD preferred.

Must have thorough working knowledge and skill using a P.C. utilizing word processing, spreadsheet, and presentation programs.

Exposure to electronic/digital blasting systems is preferred.

Experience with mine tailings and impoundment facilities is a positive

Effective decision-making and problem solving skills.

Strong administrative, organizational, and time management skills.

Must be a self-starter with the ability to work with others in a team environment.

Strong verbal, written, analytical and persuasive skills and the ability to interact effectively with all levels of employees and management.

Experience in supervising personnel is preferred.

Possession of a valid driver’s license issued by the state.

Ability to function within the qualifications outlined in the attached physical demands sheets.

Reporting Relationships

This role reports to the Technical Services Manager 

Legislative Requirements

US work permit required

Language Requirements

English

Travel Requirements

Ability and willingness to travel

Job Description

Under the general supervision of the Supervisor, the incumbent performs electrical repairs, installations, inspections and preventive maintenance of electrical lines, machinery and equipment on the mine site while continuously aligning daily functions to reflect Kinross’ values.

Job Responsibilities

•    Maintain, troubleshoot, and repair AC/DC drive systems, AC/DC motors, electrical shovel, electrical power distribution, protection systems, metering, PLC’s, and lighting systems.
• Computer manuals - Create and research existing work orders in JDE. Read, comprehend, and interpret instrumentation data sheets, schematics, P&IDs, blueprints, and instructional guides. Demonstrate basic knowledge of computers. Demonstrate the ability to load and run equipment-specific software. Demonstrate proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, & Power point). Use JDE to procure parts from the warehouse and review and enter equipment history.
•    Construction and code - Read, comprehend, and interpret the National Electric Code and install and maintain according to this guideline. Demonstrate advanced knowledge of installation and design of electrical equipment circuits up to 15 KV. Possess basic construction skills. Possess basic conduit fitting and layout skills (run rise offset, laterals, and saddles).
•    Troubleshooting and repair - Troubleshoot and repair electrical systems, including basic wiring, circuit installation, cables and switch gear up to 15 KV. Troubleshoot, repair, inspect, and install lighting fixtures, welders, grinders, and power tools. Possess basic knowledge of control systems. Troubleshoot and repair field instruments and devices.
•    Programmable logic controllers - Demonstrate general knowledge and theory of operation for a PLC. Demonstrate basic troubleshooting and repair of PLC and associated auxiliary components. Identify components of a PLC and their function. Navigate ladder logic and identify faults. Demonstrate general knowledge of DCS and auxiliary components.
•    Variable frequency drives - Demonstrate general knowledge and theory of a VFD. Troubleshoot and repair VFD and demonstrate knowledge of associated components. Identify components of a VFD and their function. Navigate the programming screen and identify faults.
•    Motors - Possess basic motor knowledge to troubleshoot, repair, inspect and install electric motors. Demonstrate general knowledge of motor control starters and associated components.
•    Instrumentation and process control - Demonstrate general knowledge of flow, pressure, temperature, level, PH, and devices. Demonstrate general knowledge of control loops - automatic, manual, and cascade. Effectively troubleshoot and repair process instruments. Demonstrate general knowledge of process circuits and their interaction with the process control instruments. Demonstrate general knowledge of control valves. Maintain accurate documentation and effective communication for installations, calibrations, and modifications of instruments.

The IT Specialist is a hands‑on, customer‑focused technologist who keeps Bald Mountain’s users productive and our site technology resilient. You’ll split time between first‑line/second‑line support and ownership of core systems: Windows servers/Active Directory, IGA (Identity Governance and Administration), Nutanix‑based virtualization and storage, Cisco switching and fiber, point‑to‑point and point‑to‑multipoint wireless links, and Dell client endpoints. You’ll also collaborate with OT and plant teams to support industrial networks and site infrastructure.

End‑user support & customer service

•    Serve as a primary contact for the North America Service Desk; resolve incidents/requests for Windows 11, Windows Server 2019 and newer, O365, Teams, Printing, VPN, and core business apps with high first‑time‑fix rates.

Server/virtualization & storage

•    Support for Cisco Desk Telephones and Teleconference Systems including Cisco desk telephones and teleconference systems.

OT & site technology

•    Partner with Operational and Support Departments on industrial networks, historian/SCADA connectivity, and change management that protects safety and uptime.

Lifecycle, documentation & compliance

•    Own device imaging/provisioning for Dell laptops/workstations; manage asset inventory and lifecycle.

On‑call & field work

•    Participate in after‑hours and weekend support rotation; travel to comm sites and facilities around the property as needed (all weather).

•    3+ years in IT support/operations with demonstrated customer service mindset.

jobs.description:

Job Summary

Kinross Round Mountain is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable and safe mining practices. We are committed to innovation and excellence in all our operations. Join our team to contribute to challenging and rewarding projects in a dynamic and supportive environment. Round Mountain is renowned as one of the most geotechnically challenging mines in Nevada.

Our Round Mountain Technical Services team is seeking an experienced Chief Underground Mining Engineer to lead the underground tech services group comprising of mine engineers, planners, surveyors, ventilation engineers, and technical technicians for the Underground Mine at Round Mountain Gold Mine. Reporting to the UG Technical Services Manager, you will ensure that the mine’s long-hope stoping mining method is designed, scheduled, and executed safely and profitably. This role will also act as the primary technical liaison between operations, geology, and management. The underground is currently in its early development stages and now transitioning from exploration development to capital development. This is a great opportunity for a motivated individual to build the foundation for the underground mining engineering group, standards, and procedures that will be used for the life of mine.  

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

• Mine Planning & Design
Develop and oversee short , mid , and long range mine plans for a long hole stoping operation using paste backfill and cemented rockfill. Approve stope designs, drill patterns, sequencing, and ground support strategies. Ensure backfill requirements (strength, timing, curing windows) are integrated into the mine schedule. Optimize stope sequencing to balance geotechnical stability, ventilation constraints, and production targets
• Technical Leadership & Team Management
Lead, mentor, and develop mine engineers, surveyors, and technical staff. Foster a collaborative environment between engineering and operations, emphasizing problem solving and continuous improvement. Set technical standards, review engineering work, and ensure quality control across all engineering deliverables.
• Operational Support
Provide real time technical guidance to underground operations, including drilling, blasting, backfilling, and ground support installation. Troubleshoot stope performance issues (dilution, overbreak, paste delivery, drilling accuracy). Coordinate with maintenance, backfill plant personnel, and production supervisors to ensure alignment with engineering plans
• Safety, Regulatory, and Environmental Compliance
Ensure all engineering designs comply with MSHA regulations and Nevada state mining requirements. Support and reinforce site Health & Safety Management Systems and environmental compliance programs. Lead risk assessments for new stopes, mining methods, or ground conditions.
• Backfill & Geotechnical Integration
Work closely with geotechnical engineers to ensure stope stability, pillar design, and sequencing meet safety and production needs. Oversee paste backfill and CRF design parameters, QA/QC, and scheduling to maintain mine stability and minimize dilution.

• Budgeting & Project Management
Manage engineering department budgets, staffing, and capital project planning. Lead or support underground capital projects (ventilation upgrades, dewatering systems, new development headings, backfill plant improvements). Evaluate and justify new technologies, equipment, or software to improve efficiency.
• Data Management & Reporting
Oversee production reporting, stope reconciliation, and variance analysis. Ensure accurate survey control, mine modeling, and engineering databases. Present engineering updates to senior leadership and contribute to life of mine planning.

Under the direction of the Maintenance Superintendent, the Underground Maintenance General Supervisor provides strategic leadership for the Underground Maintenance organization. The role leads supervisors and maintenance support resources while aligning maintenance systems, people, budgets, and asset plans with Round Mountain Gold’s underground mining objectives.

Strategic Leadership
- Develop and execute long-range maintenance strategies aligned with Underground Operations business plans, site objectives, production forecasts, and asset management requirements.

Asset Management & Reliability
- Establish fleet lifecycle, reliability, component replacement, rebuild, and condition-monitoring strategies that improve availability, control cost, and extend asset life.

Business Planning & Budgeting
-  Develop, manage, and monitor annual operating budgets, capital requests, maintenance forecasts, contractor strategies, and financial performance against approved plans.

Organizational Capability
- Build and develop a high-performing underground maintenance organization through workforce planning, succession planning, leadership development, coaching, and technical training strategy.

Underground Growth & Ramp-Up
- Provide leadership for underground startup, fleet integration, maintenance infrastructure, maintenance readiness, systems development, and scalability for future growth.

Cross-Functional Alignment
  - Partner with Mine Operations, Planning, Reliability, Engineering, Supply Chain, Safety, HR, OEMs, contractors, and site leadership to support business priorities.

Governance & KPI Ownership

•  Minimum five (5) years of progressive maintenance experience in underground hard-rock mining operations required.
•  Minimum eight (8) years of maintenance leadership experience required.
•  Minimum five (5) years leading maintenance supervisors, planners, reliability personnel, contractors, or equivalent maintenance management teams required.
•  Demonstrated experience developing and executing maintenance strategies for underground mobile mining fleets required.
•  Demonstrated experience managing operating budgets, capital budgets, maintenance cost performance, contractor strategy, and long-range maintenance forecasts required.

jobs.description:

Job Summary

The IT Specialist is a hands‑on, customer‑focused technologist who keeps Bald Mountain’s users productive and our site technology resilient. The IT Specialist will split time between first‑line/second‑line support and have ownership of core systems: Windows servers/Active Directory, IGA (Identity Governance and Administration), Nutanix‑based virtualization and storage, Cisco switching and fiber, point‑to‑point and point‑to‑multipoint wireless links, and Dell client endpoints. The IT Specialist will collaborate with OT and plant teams to support industrial networks and site infrastructure. 

Essential Functions

1.    Systems analysis techniques and procedures, including consulting with end users, contractors and vendors to determine hardware and software or system functional specifications.
2.    Design, documentation, analysis, testing of computer systems or programs, based on site and department specifications. 
3.    Serve as a primary contact for the North America Service Desk; troubleshoot and resolve incidents/requests for Windows 11, Windows Server 2019 and newer, O365, Teams, Printing, VPN, and core business apps with high first‑time‑fix rates.
4.    Provide one‑on‑one and small‑group end‑user training; write how‑to guides and knowledge base articles.
5.    Administer Windows Server/AD, DNS/DHCP, GPO, and patching; monitor backups and recovery procedures.
6.    Operate Nutanix‑based clusters (compute/storage/virtualization) and site NAS/SAN (Dell/Synology); perform capacity and health checks and coordinate upgrades with vendors.
7.    Maintain and administer campus/industrial Ethernet (Cisco) switching, VLANs, QoS, link aggregation, and optics; ensure fiber plant integrity and documentation.
8.    Support site point‑to‑point and point‑to‑multipoint wireless systems (backhaul and access), including design inputs, LOS checks, and alignment/validation.
9.    Support for Cisco Desk Telephones and Teleconference Systems including Cisco desk telephones and teleconference systems.
10.    Partner with Operational and Support Departments on industrial networks, historian/SCADA connectivity, and change management that protects safety and uptime.
11.    Own device imaging/provisioning for Dell laptops/workstations; manage asset inventory and lifecycle.
12.    Follow site safety and LOTOTO practices; complete required MSHA new‑miner training; adhere to Kinross Americas Safety Guidelines in all work.
13.    Contribute to change records and diagrams; keep runbooks, network maps, and rack elevations current.
14.    Participate in after‑hours and weekend support rotation; travel to comm sites and facilities around the property as needed (all weather).
15.    Work independently and with minimal supervision.  Present concerns and potential solution to KNV IT Leadership for decision making as appropriate.  

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

•    Advance knowledge in information technology, information systems and/or networking or 3+ years’ experience in a relevant field required.
•    Experience in IT support/operations with demonstrated customer service mindset.
•    Solid skills with Windows client/Server, AD, DNS/DHCP, GPO, and endpoint management; strong troubleshooting across OS/app/network stacks.
•    Hands‑on experience with Cisco switching and fiber (port/VLAN provisioning, SFPs, optics, link testing).
•    Working knowledge of wireless links (P2P/PMP) and fundamentals like RSSI/SNR, alignment, and link budgets.
•    Familiarity with virtualization and enterprise storage (Nutanix preferred) and backup/recovery workflows.
•    Ability to create and deliver clear user training and concise documentation.
•    Valid driver’s license; ability to safely work at heights/rack spaces and lift up to ~50 lbs; willingness to work outdoors in a mine environment.
•    Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment when handling sensitive business or personal information.
•    Commitment to ethical conduct and compliance with Kinross data protection and privacy standards

Preferred Experience

•    Certifications: CompTIA A+/Network+, CCNA, Microsoft MD‑102/Windows, AZ‑104, Nutanix NCP.
•    Experience in OT/industrial networks and CPwE concepts; exposure to SCADA/historian connectivity.

jobs.title: UG Chief Surveyor (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

Kinross Round Mountain is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable and safe mining practices. We are committed to innovation and excellence in all our operations. Join our team to contribute to challenging and rewarding projects in a dynamic and supportive environment. Round Mountain is renowned as one of the most geotechnically challenging mines in Nevada.

Our Round Mountain Technical Services team is seeking a Underground Surveyor Supervisor to lead the Underground Survey group for the Underground Mine at Round Mountain Gold Mine. Reporting to the UG Chief Mine Engineer, you will lead the underground survey department, manage survey standards and quality control, and provide accurate, timely spatial data to engineering, geology, and operations. This role will ensure that all underground workings, long-hole stopes, and infrastructure are surveyed, mapped, and reported to support safe and efficient mining. The underground is currently in its early development stages and now transitioning from exploration development to capital development. This is a great opportunity for a motivated individual to build the foundation for the underground survey group, standards, and procedures that will be used for the life of mine.  

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

•  Survey Leadership and Team Management
Lead, train, and develop the underground survey team, ensuring consistent technical performance and adherence to best practices. Assign daily and weekly survey tasks aligned with mine planning and production priorities. Maintain a culture of safety, accuracy, and continuous improvement within the survey group.
•  Underground Surveying and Data Collection
Establish and maintain underground survey control networks, including primary and secondary control points. Perform development surveys, including heading markups, line and grade, and breakthrough checks. Conduct production surveys for long hole stopes, including collaring, toe checks, and cavity monitoring. Capture as built data for development, infrastructure, and backfill operations.
•  Long-hole Stoping Support
Provide precise drill markups for long hole production drilling. Verify stope boundaries, slot raises, and breakthrough locations to minimize dilution and ensure compliance with design. Survey underground backfill boundaries to support geotechnical and engineering QA/QC.
•  Data Management and Reporting
Maintain accurate survey databases, digital models, and spatial records. Deliver timely updates to mine engineering, geology, and operations, including 3D models, maps, and progress reports. Support reconciliation of planned vs. actual development and stope performance on a regular cadence as needed (daily, weekly, monthly)
•  Technology, Equipment, and Quality Control
Oversee maintenance, calibration, and proper use of survey instruments (total stations, scanners, LiDAR, GPS for surface tie ins). Implement QA/QC procedures for all survey data and deliverables. Evaluate and adopt new survey technologies to improve accuracy and efficiency.

•  Safety, Compliance, and Regulatory Requirements
Ensure all survey activities comply with MSHA regulations and site safety standards. Participate in underground inspections, hazard identification, and risk assessments. Support environmental and operational compliance through accurate spatial documentation.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

•    Degree or diploma in Surveying, Geomatics, Mining Engineering Technology, or related field (preferred)
•    Mine surveyor certification or Professional Land Surveyor (PLS) is preferred but not always required

•    Experience in long-hole stoping environments strongly preferred
•    Proficiency with underground survey instruments and software (e.g., Leica, Trimble, Deswik)
•    Strong understanding of underground control networks, stope surveying, and 3D modeling
•    Ability to interpret engineering designs and mine plans
•    Proficient in Microsoft Software

Under the direction of the Underground Mobile Maintenance Supervisor, the Underground Mobile Maintenance Technician is responsible for safely inspecting, troubleshooting, servicing, and repairing underground mobile mining equipment in both shop and field environments. Work closely with operations, planning, warehouse, and fellow maintenance team members to minimize downtime and support reliable production. 

Demonstrate ownership of assigned equipment, tools, and tasks while consistently meeting performance, attendance, and workmanship expectations.

Strong communication, teamwork, and interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively across maintenance and operations teams required.

Bald Mountain is an important contributor to the economy of northeastern Nevada and maintains a comprehensive environmental strategy including wildlife protection, habitat recovery and education.

Job Summary

The Senior Mine Engineer (Long Range) is responsible for developing, maintaining, and optimizing the Life of Mine (LOM) plans and designs for Kinross Nevada open-pit operations. This role ensures long-term strategic plans are economically optimized, safe, and compliant with geotechnical and environmental standards. They work closely with technical services, geology, and site management to maximize shareholder value and operational performance.

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Key Responsibilities

1.    Strategic Mine Planning: Run pit optimizations and support mineral inventory reporting requirements, optimize mine plans, fleet sizing studies, create stack plans, and technical studies focused on asset optimization.
2.    Design And Modelling: Create open pits, waste rock dumps, haul roads and stormwater drainages. Able to check block models using drill data, run statistics and create scripts preferred.
3.    Scheduling and Economic Analysis: Integrates short-term plans into long-term, and life-of-mine plans. Perform excel level economic analysis. Support feasibility studies (NI 43-101) as required.
4.    Reconciliation and Compliance: Analyzes and interprets mine plans to ensure alignment with financial, environmental and operational objectives. Perform reconciliation of actuals vs. planned production, updating plans to reflect reality while maximizing NPV.
5.    Collaboration: Work with short range planners, environmental, exploration, metallurgy, geotech, maintenance, and leadership teams to ensure long term plans are technically sound.
6.    Innovation: Researches information to support decision-making and improve processes, technologies or methodologies.
7.    Safety and Mentorship: Contributes to safety culture, and the development of policies and practices. Must be willing to take on cross-rotation assignments within the Technical Services Group for personal development.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1.    B.S. Degree in Mining or related discipline.
2.    5 Years of experience in surface mining preferred.
3.    Comprehensive knowledge of the principles and concepts of open pit mining engineering.  
4.    General understanding of mining operations, as well as limited understanding of milling and maintenance operations.

jobs.title: Superintendent, Open Pit (Red Lake, ON, CA)
jobs.description:
The Great Bear project is a development-stage asset located in the renowned and prolific Red Lake mining district, and represents one of the most exciting recent gold discoveries globally.  The project has excellent potential to become a top-tier deposit that could support a large, long-life mine complex. Kinross’ comprehensive exploration and development program will aim to support the vision of a quality, high-grade, open-pit mine and a longer-term, sizeable underground mine.

Job Summary

The Superintendent, Open Pit will be responsible for overseeing the safe, efficient, and cost-effective execution of all open pit mining activities, including drilling, blasting, loading, and hauling operations. This position provides leadership and direction to operational teams, ensuring production targets are achieved in alignment with short and long term mine plans, budget, and engineering standards. The Superintendent is accountable for the safety, performance, and development of the open pit team and for managing the area operating budget and resources to meet operational objectives.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

Oversee and direct open pit mining operations, ensuring safe, efficient execution of drilling, blasting, loading, and hauling activities to achieve production targets.

Lead and coordinate short to medium term operational plans, ensuring alignment between engineering designs and field execution.

Collaborate with Technical Services to review and implement mine plans and schedules and analyze and address deviations from plans.

Ensure effective coordination between Mining, Maintenance, Processing, and Technical Services teams to meet site objectives.

Oversee drill and blast and haulage activities to ensure plans are executed safely and in accordance with Kinross, Great Bear standards.

Mange the pit operation to ensure production targets are achieved and within expected ore grade targets and use all available tools to drive continuous improvement.

Develop medium to long term forecasting plans (people, equipment) to effectively execute operational targets.

Assist with the preparation of annual budgets and business plans and manage operational costs

Collaborate with Senior Leadership, Technical Services, Maintenance, and other support departments.

Coordinate workforce planning, training, and succession development.

Provide leadership, coaching, and mentorship to supervision and production crews, leading by example and visibly putting health and safety first to build a strong safety culture.

Set performance targets and KPIs and monitor, measure, and manage the performance of the team and direct reports.

Work in a healthy work environment with full support, cooperation, and commitment to satisfy our operation’s goal of being accident-free.

Support a work environment that is aligned with Kinross’ Safeground principles and promote Principles across all work areas.

Comply with federal and provincial acts and regulations, and legal requirements.

Adhere to all relevant Great Bear policies and procedures.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

A bachelor’s degree in mining engineering or a related technical discipline (or an equivalent combination of education and experience), with 10+ years of progressive open pit mining experience, including at least 3 years in a superintendent or senior supervisory role.

Experience in open pit operations and demonstrated leadership in a previous open pit start-up is preferred. A Professional Engineering designation (P.Eng. with Professional Engineers Ontario, or eligibility to register) is considered a strong asset.

Strong understanding of mine planning, scheduling, and production processes.

Experience with grade control, reconciliation, and operational reporting.

Demonstrated leadership and team management experience.

High attention to detail with excellent organizational skills.

Benefits

At Kinross, Great Bear, we are committed to Putting People First by fostering employee growth and development, celebrating achievements, and rewarding team success. Benefits offered for this position include: 

Annual Fitness and Mental Health Reimbursement

Employee Share Purchase Plan, Registered Retirement Savings, and Registered Pension Plans

160 Hours of Paid Vacation

Employee Assistance Program

Employee Recognition Program

Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance

Life, Accidental Death & Dismemberment, and Disability Insurance

Training and Development Opportunities

Relocation assistance may be provided to eligible candidates on a case-by-case basis

Work Conditions

This position is based in Red Lake, Ontario. Local candidates, or those willing to relocate, with relocation assistance, will be given priority for this position. The schedule for this position is 5X2.

Compensation and Total Rewards

The base salary for the Superintendent, Open Pit is $175,000.00 to $210,000.00 + Short Term Incentive, + Long Term Incentive, + Group Benefit Coverage. 

The hiring range reflects our targeted compensation framework for the role. The actual offer will be determined through a comprehensive evaluation of each candidate's experience, capabilities, and potential impact, along with consideration of internal equity, team structure, and benchmark market data for similar positions. In addition to base salary, Kinross offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support employee well-being, performance, and long-term development. 

Use of AI in Our Hiring Process

We use AI-enabled tools to help sort and review applications based on job-related criteria. All hiring decisions, including who moves forward in the process, are made by a human.

jobs.title: Chief Geologist (Elko, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Bald Mountain is an open-pit mine with a large estimated mineral resource in the largest private mining land package in the U.S. The mine is located in White Pine County, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world, along the southern extension of the prolific Carlin trend. Bald Mountain and the nearby Round Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

Bald Mountain is an important contributor to the economy of northeastern Nevada and maintains a comprehensive environmental strategy including wildlife protection, habitat recovery and education.

Job Summary

The Chief Geologist is responsible for providing leadership in Geology to technical service group, the mining department and mining contractors to ensure that the mine functions effectively and safely.  To maintain and support procedures and work practices aimed at preventing accidents or injuries.  

Essential Functions

1.  Develop geotechnical design criteria to support safe and optimal mine operations.
2.  Supervise Ore Control and Sampling to support mine planning, mine operations and projects.
3.  Make recommendations on ground control performance to guarantee safe operation and to optimize ore deposit recovery.
4.  Proactively perform site inspections.
5.  Supervise Resource modelling and estimations.
6.  Plan and budget infill and exploration drilling programs.
7.  Supervise plan and budget for Geology requirements.   
8.  Coordinate the mine planning short term and medium term material estimations 
9.  Develop, maintain and update structural and geology models.
10.  Effectively communicate geology outcomes.
11.  Provide comprehensive and timely contributions to the daily, weekly, monthly and annual reports.
12.  Improve the overall safety performance of the site including facilitating Job Safety Analyses and Incident Analyses.
13.  Train and mentor engineer, geologist and hydrogeologist in all aspects of Geology.
14.  Compliance with all company policies and procedures including, but not limited to safety, environmental, confidentiality, and code of conduct.
15.  Punctuality and regular attendance required. 
16.  Perform other related functions as assigned by Technical Services Manager.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

1.  Bachelor degree in Geology.
2.  A postgraduate Degree in Geology is preferred. 
3.  Candidates should have a minimum of 8 years of Geology experience in metal mining.
4.  Hydrology and Geotech experience is desirable.
5.  Practical experience with ore control and sampling techniques.
6.  Experience in Resource modelling.
7.  Understanding on leach and flotation ore processing techniques.
8.  Understanding of rock mass strength, structural characterization and slope stability controls. 
9.  A high level of computer literacy with specialized software such as Leapfrog is needed.
10.  Computer literacy with specialized mining software is needed.
11.  Effective written and oral communication skills.
12.  Effective decision making and problem solving skills.
13.  Must have the ability to plan, coordinate and schedule time to achieve overall objectives.
14.  Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to delegate.
15.  Must possess a valid driver’s license.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•   Adheres to all safety and environmental considerations.
•   Have a strong commitment to safe working practices. 
•   Wears Personal Protective Equipment at all times while in the production environment. 
•   Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions.

jobs.title: Underground Geology Intern (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

The position is intended to provide a university student studying geology with practical work experience in underground mining while assisting the geology team with routine operational geology duties and special projects. The intern will gain exposure to underground development, production, grade control, geological data collection, and core or chip logging while consistently demonstrating Kinross values.

Essential Functions

1.  Assists underground geologists with development heading mapping, face and back mapping, geological interpretation, and underground grade control activities.
2.  Assists with underground mapping and sampling programs, including face, rib, back, muck, channel, and development sampling as assigned.
3.  Supports collection and documentation of structural, geotechnical, groundwater, and ground-condition observations encountered in underground headings and excavations.
4.  Assists with underground diamond, reverse-circulation, long hole, or other drilling programs through drill monitoring, core or chip handling, recovery measurements, orientation checks, sampling, and documentation as assigned.
5.  Assist underground geologists with special projects such as stope reconciliation, dilution and ore-loss reviews, muck movement tracking, cavity monitoring data review, paste or backfill sampling support, and underground water-quality sampling.
6.  Performs sample preparation, labeling, chain-of-custody documentation, quality-assurance and quality-control checks, cataloging, and secure storage tasks.
7.  Works collaboratively with geology, mine operations, engineering, survey, and technical services personnel to complete assigned duties and communicate geological observations.

We are seeking a skilled and experienced Senior Geologist to lead our Ore Control geology team. This individual will play a pivotal role in guiding the team’s professional growth, validating geological data, collaborating on material routing strategies, managing the minex drilling program and upholding safety excellence. The ideal candidate will possess a deep understanding of geology, strong leadership qualities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

•  Guide and nurture the professional growth of the ore control geology team, providing mentorship and training to enhance their skills. Establish and manage individual development plans for team members.

•  Collaborate with the operations group to develop material routing strategies, particularly focusing on addressing geometallurgical challenges to optimize processing efficiency.

•  Conduct end-of-month and site reconciliation report, meticulously identifying discrepancies and devising practical solutions to address them, thus minimizing production variances.

•  Drive a culture of continuous improvement within the geology department, actively seeking out opportunities to enhance efficiency, quality, and effectiveness.
•  Conduct rigorous validation of block models to ensure accuracy and reliability of geological data for operational and planning purposes.
•  Engage closely with the corporate Technical Service team on various projects and the Life of Mine (LOM) plan, fostering synergy and alignment between technical functions and corporate objectives.
•  Oversee and manage laboratory Ore Control samples quality assurance and quality control processes, ensuring the integrity and reliability of analytical results.
•  Define and control the minex drilling program, ensuring its effective execution, and maintaining regular communication with the exploration team to monitor progress and adjust strategies as needed.

Provide oversight of contracts and contractors related to site services’ areas of responsibility.

jobs.title: Process Control Engineer (Round Mountain, NV, US)
jobs.description:
Round Mountain is an open-pit mine located in Nevada, one of the best mining jurisdictions in the world. The mine uses conventional open-pit mining methods and processes ore by mill and heap leach. Kinross began operating the mine in 2003, and it has since become a continuous improvement leader in the Company’s portfolio. Round Mountain poured its 15 millionth ounce in 2018. Round Mountain and the nearby Bald Mountain mine make up Kinross’ Nevada operations. 

The Round Mountain mine is an important contributor to the Nye County economy and, working with local stakeholders, has helped achieve significant improvements in healthcare and education in the area.

Job Summary

The Process Control Engineer is responsible for developing, maintaining, and optimizing process control systems that support safe, reliable, and efficient mineral processing operations at the Round Mountain Gold Mine. This role focuses on improving plant stability, throughput, recovery, and equipment performance through effective control strategies, automation enhancements, and close collaboration with operations, metallurgy, and maintenance teams.

Qualified candidates may be eligible for both a sign-on bonus and relocation assistance.

Essential Functions

Process Control & Automation
•    Design, implement, maintain, and optimize control strategies for crushing, grinding, classification, leaching, adsorption, detoxification, and ancillary systems as applicable.
•    Configure, troubleshoot, and support plant control systems (e.g., DCS, PLCs, HMI/SCADA) to ensure high system availability and reliability.
•    Develop and tune regulatory, advanced, and model-based control loops to improve process stability and metallurgical performance.
•    Lead and support control system upgrades, logic changes, alarm management, and interface improvements in accordance with site change management procedures.
Operational Support
•    Partner with Operations and Metallurgy to identify process constraints and variability, and implement control solutions that improve throughput, recovery, and reagent efficiency.
•    Provide on-shift and off-shift technical support for control system issues impacting production or safety.
•    Analyze process data and trends to proactively identify opportunities for improvement and risk mitigation.
Maintenance & Reliability Interface
•    Work closely with the Process Maintenance Superintendent and maintenance teams to support instrumentation, control hardware, and network reliability.
•    Support preventative maintenance strategies, control system documentation, and lifecycle management of automation assets.
•    Assist with root cause analysis for process upsets and equipment or control-related failures.
Safety, Compliance & Standards
•    Promote a strong safety culture by ensuring control systems support safe operating limits and critical safeguards.
•    Participate in hazard analyses, management of change (MOC), and operational readiness reviews.
Projects & Continuous Improvement
•    Provide process control expertise for capital projects, plant modifications, and technology trials.
•    Develop functional specifications, FAT/SAT documentation, and commissioning plans for automation-related projects.
•    Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives focused on cost reduction, energy efficiency, and operational excellence.

Qualifications and Skill Requirements

•    Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Automation, or a related discipline.
•    5–8 years of experience in process control or automation within mineral processing, mining, or heavy industrial environments.
•    Familiarity with CMMS 
•    Hands-on experience with DCS and/or PLC platforms commonly used in mining operations (e.g., Honeywell, ABB, Emerson, Rockwell).
•    Strong understanding of mineral processing unit operations and their control requirements.
•    Control loop tuning, alarm management, and control system troubleshooting.
•    Process data analysis and visualization tools (e.g., Wonderware, PI System or equivalent historians).
•    Instrumentation fundamentals, including flow, level, pressure, density, and analytical measurements.
•    Familiarity with advanced process control (APC) concepts is preferred.
•    Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
•    Ability to work effectively across operations, maintenance, and technical disciplines.
•    Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts into operational guidance.

Health, Safety, and Environmental Requirements

•    Has a strong commitment to Environmental, health and safety.
•    Wears Personal Protective Equipment at all times while in the production environment.
•    Is alert and observes, corrects, and reports unsafe conditions and behaviors.

Gestionar las actividades relacionadas a la ingeniería en calidad, costo y tiempo, considerando la etapa de los proyectos desde su etapa conceptual hasta su ejecución, garantizando el cumplimiento de los estándares de diseño para que los proyectos sean seguros y económicos.

jobs.description:
*Descripción de la empresa*

Andeantek es una firma especializada de ingeniería y tecnología enfocada en el procesamiento avanzado de minerales, el desarrollo de proyectos y la comercialización de concentrados para el sector minero andino, que forma parte de un grupo empresarial de alcance global con presencia en Asia, Europa, Norteamérica y Australasia. Combinando una profunda experiencia en el diseño de concentradoras de cobre y oro con tecnologías de punta asistidas por campos físicos, Andeantek acompaña a sus clientes desde la etapa de concepto hasta la implementación de plantas a nivel de laboratorio, piloto y escala industrial. Responsable de la planificación, supervisión y seguimiento de las operaciones de producción en la planta de chancado, asegurando el cumplimiento de los objetivos de producción, calidad, seguridad y gestión ambiental establecidos por la Gerencia.

* Scheduling de producción.

* Mitigar riesgos y tomar en cuenta el impacto ambiental.

_Entre otras responsabilidades que sean relevantes para el tipo de puesto._

*Requisitos*

* Residir en Trujillo o tener estadía*(Imprescindible)*.
* Mínimo 1 año de experiencia.
* Máximo 5 años de experiencia.
* Carreras Tecnicas de Supervisión de producción o Ingeniero Industrial, Ingeniero Mécanico, Ingeniero Metalúrgico, entre otras similares.

CONTACTO:

Enviar su CV al siguiente correo electronico: gl@andeantek.com

jobs.title: Geólogo(a) Senior de Perforación
jobs.description:
¡SOMOS TALENTOS SIN ETIQUETAS!

En Las Bambas nos ocupamos por tener una cultura diversa e inclusiva, promoviendo un ambiente seguro en el que todas las personas, sin distinción, se sientan respetadas, valoradas y capaces de generar valor a la compañía desde su rol. Para conocer más acerca de nosotros y nuestra cultura, visite nuestra página web:
https://www.lasbambas.com/es

¿QUÉ RETO TENDRÁS?

Supervisar la ejecución de los programas de exploración minera e identificación de nuevos blancos con potencial para descubrir recursos minerales económicos, asegurando la integridad, calidad y confiabilidad de la información geocientífica y de las bases de datos de exploración, de acuerdo con los estándares corporativos y las mejores prácticas de la industria, con la finalidad de agregar valor a Minera Las Bambas y contribuir al crecimiento de MMG.

¿CÓMO GENERARÁS VALOR DESDE TU ROL?

Elaborar y planificar: Alcances, costos, tiempo y requerimiento de personal de los programas de perforación diamantina en el tajo Ferrobamba y proyectos chalcobamba y sulfobamba, para mejorar la categoría e incrementar recursos.

Control y seguimiento, durante la etapa de la ejecución y/o perforación de los programas de perforación diamantina.

Administración de contratos desde la etapa de la licitación hasta el cierre del contrato de: Perforación diamantina, construcción de plataformas, personal técnico de apoyos (controladores y conductores), medición de desviación y orientación de máquinas.

Coordinar la asistencia de la supervisión a las reuniones de Operación, trabajos en sala de logueo y de voladura.

Asegurar las firmas y supervisión de los documentos de gestión de seguridad de los contratistas a cargo antes del inicio de actividades.

Supervisión de máquinas de perforación en todos los frentes de trabajo, Ferrobamba, Chalcobamba.

Gestión de construcción y entrega de plataformas de perforación, cumpliendo con el formato de entrega de plataformas.

Supervisión de trabajos realizados por los geólogos y técnicos en la sala de logueo y almacén de testigos a cargo de la contratista de turno.

Revisión y validación de la información generada por los geólogos de mina, por ejemplo: Logueo geológico, mapeo superficial, survey, collar e interpretación de secciones geológicas, etc.

Coordinar con las diferentes áreas Operativas de Mina, SSTT, RRCC, Servicios Generales, etc. Respecto a los permisos necesarios de los diferentes alcances del programa de perforación diamantina.

Diseñar y elaborar programas semanales y mensuales de perforación diamantina y construcción de plataformas.

Supervisar, entrenar y dar coaching a equipo de geólogos de mina.

Control y seguimiento del presupuesto anual de CAPEX de: Perforación diamantina, construcción de plataformas y personal técnico de apoyo (controladores y conductores).

Revisar y validar los procedimientos y PETS de las tareas.

Cumplir con los KPI de seguridad según el estándar de MMG.

Liderar las investigaciones de incidentes hasta completar los planes de acción generados y su cierre en el SAP.

Crear un buen ambiente laboral en el área.

Ingeniero Geólogo colegiado.

Especialización deseable en Geología, Geoquímica, Geología Económica, Geología de Exploración, o alguna especialidad relacionada.

Post Grado deseable: Maestría en gestión minera u otros.

Mínimo 8 años de experiencia en Exploración Geológica y Perforación o en posiciones similares.

MS Office (Word, Excel, Power Point, project, outlook etc)

Vulcan, Minesight, Gis y software de base de datos.

Sólidos conocimientos de la geología de yacimientos del tipo pórfido y skarn

Gestión de Proyectos (inicio, planificación, control- seguimiento y cierre)

Supervisión de perforación diamantina

Control y seguimiento de presupuesto de programas de perforación diamantina.

Conocimiento de técnicas de: Logueo y descripción geológica, Cartografiado geológico, muestreo, interpretación de secciones geológicas en 2D y modelo geológico.

jobs.title: Tecnico Topografo - Sector Minero
jobs.description: TÉCNICO TOPÓGRAFO – SECTOR MINEROEn Manpower Perú buscamos al mejor talento para asumir el reto como Técnico Topógrafo, para importante empresa del sector minero. ¡La oportunidad de impulsar tu carrera está aquí!OBJETIVO DE LA POSICIÓN: Realizar el levantamiento topográfico en interior mina, en labores de avance, explotación y superficie, con la finalidad de asegurar la información actualizada en CAD y Datamine, para controlar la ejecución y elaboración de proyectos mineros.RESPONSABILIDADES Y FUNCIONES: Actualizar planos de trabajo en CAD para el seguimiento de proyectos según los planes de minado mensuales. Realizar la medición de avances lineales, rotura de mineral y cubicación de mineral, con seguimiento semanal y mensual. Realizar levantamientos con estación total y dron, junto con la ejecución de poligonales para el control de precisión en mina. Elaborar el modelamiento topográfico en 3D de acuerdo a los levantamientos en campo. Realizar el marcado de proyectos de avances, proyectos de perforación en tajos y proyectos de DDH. Realizar el levantamiento de stock de canchas y procesamiento de información. Realizar el levantamiento de desviación de taladros con el Boretrack. Conducir una camioneta 4x4 para el cumplimiento de las funciones asignadas. Cumplir y hacer cumplir las normas del Reglamento Interno de Trabajo, Seguridad y de los sistemas de gestión aplicables a su unidad. Colaborar y/o apoyar en cualquier otra actividad complementaria afín a su puesto que le sea encomendada por su jefe.REQUISITOS Técnico en Topografía, 3 años de estudios (Indispensable). Estudios en topografía subterránea (Deseable). Experiencia mínima de 6 años en minería, 3 años en posiciones similares (Indispensable). Microsoft Office Intermedio. (Indispensable). AutoCAD Avanzado. (Indispensable). Datamine Intermedio (Indispensable). Conocimiento en topografía, geometría descriptiva o de espacio, matemática, aritmética y trigonometría (Indispensable). Licencia A2B con 3 años de antigüedad. (Indispensable). 2 años de experiencia manejando camioneta 4x4 en interior mina, sin faltas (Indispensable). Conocimientos en Seguridad: peligros y riesgos asociados a las operaciones; procedimientos e instructivos de seguridad y salud ocupacional relacionados con las operaciones de la empresa. Conocimientos en Medio Ambiente: aspectos e impactos ambientales asociados a las operaciones; procedimientos e instructivos de gestión ambiental relacionados con las operaciones de la empresa.BENEFICIOS Formar parte de una importante empresa del sector minero. Ingreso a planilla directa de nuestro cliente, con todos los beneficios conforme indica ley.En Manpower Perú, promovemos la inclusión e inserción laboral sin distinción por razón de discapacidad, género, orientación, identidad y expresión de género, lugar de origen o generación. Por ello, ¡todos los talentos son bienvenidos!

jobs.description: Misión u objetivo: Brindar soporte técnico-operativo en la preparación, manipulación y aplicación de productos de voladura en minería subterránea, asegurando la correcta ejecución de los procedimientos establecidos, el cumplimiento de estándares de seguridad y la satisfacción del cliente. jobs.title: Especialista de Aprendizaje
jobs.description:
Anglo American, en sociedad con la Corporación Mitsubishi, está desarrollando la operación minera Quellaveco, uno de los yacimientos de cobre más grandes del mundo, localizado en la región de Moquegua, al sur del Perú.

Quellaveco tendrá una vida de reservas de 30 años. Utilizará proceso minero de tajo abierto y flotación para producir concentrados de cobre, así como molibdeno y plata como subproductos. Se espera que Quellaveco produzca en promedio 300 mil toneladas de cobre por año en sus primeros 10 años de operación.

En Anglo American nuestra estrategia es asegurar y desarrollar Quellaveco aplicando prácticas y tecnologías innovadoras que confiamos a nuestra gente. Estamos comprometidos a convertirnos en socios para el futuro, operar con seguridad, sustentabilidad y responsabilidad.

En Anglo American nos encontramos en búsqueda de un
Especialista de Aprendizaje
para ser parte de nuestro gerencia de Talento, Desarrollo y Cultura.

Objetivo principal

Diseñar, implementar y gestionar la propuesta integral de aprendizaje de Anglo American Quellaveco, asegurando el desarrollo de las capacidades técnicas críticas requeridas para la operación, mediante la identificación de brechas de competencias, el diseño de soluciones de aprendizaje, programas de desarrollo, entrenamiento cruzado, formación normativa, etc. Además, de la gestión de proveedores especializados y la articulación con líderes de la operación que permitan asegurar la eficiencia y efectividad de todas las iniciativas.

Funciones principales

Identificar, evaluar y planificar las prioridades de desarrollo de competencias técnicas que contribuyan a los objetivos operacionales asegurando además la alineación entre los requerimientos y las prioridades, tiempos y recursos de la organización.

Diseñar y desplegar acciones que contribuyan a la evaluación y cierre de brechas técnicas operacionales alineado a las necesidades actuales y futuras.

Asegurar la alineación de los programas internos de desarrollo de competencias técnicas con la estrategia de desarrollo de talento, posiciones críticas, sucesión y programas externos de desarrollo.

Coordinar y asegurar la implementación de contratos de servicios de aprendizaje técnicos con KPIs definidos y reportes periódicos de calidad, desviaciones y mejores prácticas.

Identificar, hacer seguimiento y reportar los KPIs relevantes que aseguren el progreso, cumplimiento de los objetivos y utilización de recursos (tiempo/presupuestos) según y acorde a los planes anuales a través del monitoreo del cierre de brechas técnicas, la efectividad de las soluciones de desarrollo, la calidad de los servicios, la utilización eficiente de recursos y la ejecución presupuestal, implementando acciones de mejora continua que fortalezcan las capacidades críticas requeridas por la operación.

Evaluar la competencia técnica de los colaboradores en los procesos de promoción interna, movilidad interna, sucesión, alineado a los criterios de desempeño esperados.

Explorar las mejores prácticas en el desarrollo de competencias técnicas que contribuyan a crecimiento organizacional y estandarizar procesos de trabajo seguro

Asegurar la actualización permanente frente a cambios tecnológicos o regulatorios alineados al modelo operativo

Monitorear y gestionar las competencias respecto a los estándares técnicos locales y globales en coordinación con las áreas operativas y equipos relevantes (seguridad, riesgos, compliance, etc).

Impulsar la incorporación y uso de plataformas digitales, analítica de datos, simuladores, inteligencia artificial y otras tecnologías de aprendizaje que contribuyan a mejorar la experiencia del usuario, la trazabilidad de las competencias técnicas y la efectividad de los programas de desarrollo.

Formación

Profesional en Ingeniería Industrial, Administración y/o carreras afines.

Deseable especialización en gestión del aprendizaje, desarrollo de rutas de aprendizaje técnico o mejora continua.

Deseable conocer herramientas digitales que permitan optimizar la gestión de aprendizaje.

Inglés nivel intermedio (deseable)

Trayectoria laboral y conocimientos

Al menos 05 años en posiciones similares relacionadas a gestión del conocimiento o capacitación

Experiencia en diseño e implementación de programas de desarrollo de habilidades técnicas

Experiencia gestionando a líderes de las áreas operativas

Experiencia en la administración de proveedores externos gestionando el desempeño, calidad y progreso de los planes e indicadores.

Conocimiento en procesos de evaluación, validación y cierre de brechas

Base: Lima

Régimen: 5x2

Contrato: Permanente

jobs.title: Supervisor, Asset Health
jobs.description:
Elk Valley Resources (EVR) operates four steelmaking coal mines that employ over 5,000 people in the Elk Valley of British Columbia. We are committed to responsible resource development, environmental performance and building strong partnerships with communities and Indigenous Peoples.

EVR is proud to be part of the Glencore Group, contributing to a global portfolio of operations with a history that dates back more than 100 years in Canada

.

Are you looking for a new career opportunity? Join our team.

Application Deadline: October 13, 2026

What we offer:

At EVR, we're dedicated to supporting our workforce on their unique career journeys.

EVR recognizes our employees' skills, competencies, and performance and offers opportunities with competitive compensation and benefits. We also aim to promote employee health and wellness and provide opportunities for professional development.

We believe in the power of diversity and strive each day to create a workplace where each individual is valued and respected for their contributions.

We also believe that our employees are the reason we are accomplishing great things and are committed to supporting them through our many different programs.

About the role:

Reporting to Supervisor, Mobile Maintenance, the Supervisor, Asset Health is responsible for maximizing equipment availability and reliability in an open-pit mining operation through real-time asset health monitoring, failure analysis, and maintenance leadership. This role leverages telemetry, condition monitoring, and operational data to identify emerging equipment issues, support troubleshooting and repair triage, and optimize maintenance strategies for both operator-driven and autonomous mining equipment. The Supervisor, Asset Health serves as a key liaison between Mining and Maintenance teams, ensuring timely communication of equipment health risks and opportunities to improve performance.

We are looking for a highly motivated individual with the ability to evaluate complex equipment health information, make informed decisions, and prioritize maintenance actions to minimize operational risk.

To be successful we are looking for someone with strong communication and relationship-building skills, as well as professionalism, integrity, and the ability to thrive in a dynamic environment where priorities may change rapidly. A commitment to maintenance excellence, innovation, technology, and continuous improvement is essential.

Join us in the breathtaking Elk Valley of British Columbia. Here you will find outdoor adventure at your fingertips. Whether it's biking and skiing, or the laid-back atmosphere of fishing and hiking, there is something for everyone! Come experience what work life balance is all about! This role will operate on a 4x4 schedule rotation

Two Annual Bonus Plans

Comprehensive Benefits Plan

Retirement Package

Health Lifestyle Account

Relocation Assistance

Participate in and adhere to health and safety programs and policies

Monitor real-time equipment telemetry, condition monitoring data, trends, and alarms to identify asset health risks and potential failure modes

Make informed maintenance intervention decisions to optimize equipment performance, reliability, and availability

Support problem-solving, diagnostic analysis, and repair triage for mobile mining assets

Review asset failure trends and support defect elimination, reliability improvement initiatives, and maintenance strategy optimization

Supervise a team of technicians responsible for diagnostics, preventive maintenance inspections, and asset repairs

Collaborate closely with maintenance planning to prioritize and schedule corrective actions and planned maintenance activities

Identify pending failures that can be proactively planned and scheduled to minimize downtime

Provide feedback to equipment operators on Operator Driven Reliability (ODR) practices and performance, while monitoring autonomous haul truck performance indicators and incorporating both operator and system feedback into asset health assessments

Facilitate communication between Operations, Maintenance, and Reliability teams regarding equipment condition, performance, and operational risks

High School Diploma and Journeyperson’s ticket, or related technical diploma or degree

Mechanical and/or electrical maintenance experience with Komatsu haul trucks and Komatsu (P&H) rope shovels is highly desirable

Experience with engine diagnostics, particularly Cummins systems, is an asset

Experience with asset health monitoring, condition monitoring, and predictive maintenance systems

Proficient computer skills, particularly in OEM systems, and proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and SAP S/4HANA

MLA Certification considered an asset

Valid Class 5 Driver’s License or equivalent

jobs.title: Ingeniero(a) de Hidrogeología IV (senior) - Cusco
jobs.description: Hudbay Perú cuenta con los más altos estándares de excelencia operacional: Seguridad y Salud Ocupacional, Medio Ambiente y Responsabilidad Social. Nuestra gestión está diseñada por personas que crean valor compartido y beneficios sostenibles a todos nuestros grupos de interés, a través de la práctica de nuestros valores corporativos porque somos responsables, expertos, dinámicos y nos sentimos orgullosos de nuestra cultura.Estamos en la búsqueda de profesionales talentosos de diferentes especialidades que busquen sus propios desafíos y oportunidades de crecimiento en el sector más importante de nuestro país. ¡Atrévete a desarrollar tu talento en Hudbay Perú!INGENIERO(A) DE HIDROGEOLOGÍA IV - CuscoPropósito:Administrar y gestionar los recursos hidrogeológicos en los diferentes componentes de la operación minera y control de presupuesto y seguimiento de la procura (materiales e insumos).Principales Funciones: Revisar y validar los planes de desagüe de minas (despresurización mediante pozos verticales y drenes subhorizontales), manejo de aguas, campañas de perforación, balance de agua mensual, actualización y calibración del modelamiento numérico con software especializado y ubicación de líneas de descarga, de acuerdo con el forecast anual de la gerencia de servicios técnicos, asegurando la estabilidad geotécnica. Supervisar y gestionar los trabajos de compensación y calidad de agua según el cronograma. Revisar los reportes semanales y mensuales de hidrogeología y validar la interpretación de la red de piezómetros (VWP y Casagrande) de los diferentes componentes mineros críticos: tajos, relavera (TMF) y depósitos de desmonte (WRFCP). Asegurar que las presiones de poro y niveles freáticos estén dentro de los umbrales de diseño. Coordinar con Geotecnia y compartir las interpretaciones. Elaborar y validar los TDR (Términos de Referencia) y criterios de diseño para los diferentes servicios hidrogeológicos: perforación y equipamiento de pozos de bombeo profundo, diseño e instalación de piezómetros, pruebas de bombeo, sistemas de mantenimiento de pozos y cambios de líneas eléctricas. Realizar la planificación, justificación técnica y seguimiento de la adquisición (procura) de infraestructura hidrogeológica: bombas sumergibles, tableros, tuberías, piezómetros (sensores, cables, dataloggers) y sistemas de telemetría, asegurando el cumplimiento de las especificaciones técnicas. Aprobar valorizaciones de empresas contratistas (perforistas, consultoras) e informes técnicos de ingeniería (diseños de pozos, reportes de pruebas hidráulicas, reportes de instalación de instrumentación y modelos hidrogeológicos). Brindar asesoría hidrogeológica estratégica y vinculante para áreas afines como Operaciones Mina (interacción de minado vs. dewatering), Medio Ambiente (monitoreo de calidad de agua y filtraciones/seepage), Relaciones Comunitarias (impacto en manantiales), Geotecnia (factores de seguridad), así como Construcción y Planta de Procesos (abastecimiento de agua). jobs.title: Cadista
jobs.description:
1. Resumen del Puesto

El *Cadista / Modelador 3D* será responsable de elaborar, actualizar y gestionar los planos, mapas topográficos y modelos tridimensionales de las operaciones mineras. Su trabajo integrará datos de planeamiento y geología, asegurando la precisión técnica necesaria para guiar de manera segura y eficiente la explotación en *minas subterráneas convencionales*.

2. Requisitos Básicos

* *Formación Académica:* Técnico o Bachiller en Topografía, Dibujo Técnico, Ingeniería de Minas, Ingeniería Geológica o carreras afines.
* *Experiencia Mínima: 1 A* *2 años de experiencia* demostrable en posiciones similares dentro del sector minero.
* *Experiencia Sectorial:* Trabajo previo indispensable en *minas convencionales* (subterránea de métodos convencionales o tajo abierto tradicional), con un fuerte entendimiento de las dinámicas de *planeamiento y geología*.

3. Competencias Técnicas (Indispensables)

* *AutoCAD / Civil 3D:* Dominio avanzado para el diseño de galerías, accesos, secciones, componentes mineros y manejo de nubes de puntos.
* *ArcGIS (u otro GIS similar):* Nivel intermedio-avanzado para la gestión de bases de datos geoespaciales, elaboración de mapas temáticos, planos de concesiones y análisis territorial.
* *Modelamiento en 3D:* Experiencia sólida en la creación de sólidos y superficies tridimensionales (vías, tajos, labores subterráneas, botaderos). Se valorará el manejo de software especializado como Datamine, Leapfrog, MineSight (Hexagon) o Deswik.

4. Funciones Principales

* Digitalizar y modelar las estructuras geológicas, vetas y cuerpos mineralizados en 3D a partir de los datos de muestreo y logueo técnico.
* Elaborar planos de secciones geológicas, plantas e interpolaciones espaciales.
* Diseñar y actualizar los planos de minado a corto, mediano y largo plazo bajo las directrices del equipo de ingeniería.
* Calcular volúmenes de extracción, avances de galerías, cubicaciones y movimientos de tierras mediante herramientas de modelado 3D.

5. Habilidades Blandas

* *Atención al detalle:* Precisión rigurosa en el manejo de coordenadas, escalas y datos numéricos.
* *Trabajo en equipo:* Coordinación constante con geólogos, ingenieros de planeamiento y topógrafos de campo.
* *Adaptabilidad:* Capacidad para responder rápidamente a los cambios y actualizaciones del diseño de mina según las condiciones del terreno.
